questions.question: When slowing or stopping, should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only when the road is wet.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A driver merging may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
It is hard for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists should never ride in pairs. Each rider needs enough space to move around and avoid hazards.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes but not your face.
Neither your eyes nor your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Where do motorcyclists have the greatest conflict with other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: The driver will not necessarily yield to you.
The driver will always yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will not necessarily yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists without actually noticing them.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake supply?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What lane position is best?

options.text: One that reduces your safety space and lets others see you.
One that increases your safety space and lets others see you.
One that increases hazards and lets others share your lane.
One that reduces hazards and lets you follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your safety space and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: The right lane position should give you more space to avoid hazards and make you more visible to others. It should keep other drivers from trying to share your lane and give you room to escape if danger appears. Choose a position that gives you the most safety space.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
You don't need to worry about it.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which sign is usually rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. These signs show traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.explanation: Good rain suits for motorcycles will not tear or balloon when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of crashing, you should:
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, be as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Gently use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep your motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid road hazards, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles allows you:

options.text: Room to move if another driver makes a mistake.
To not react to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Room to move if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and move if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move between different parts of your lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane unsafely.

questions.question: Which of the following will not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Proper protection includes an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and sturdy clothing.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front end.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet or slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: When making a regular stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. This habit makes it easier to brake hard in an emergency. Practice using both brakes every time.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: See better and be seen better.

questions.explanation: Your lane position helps your safety in several ways. It helps you see better and be seen better, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal, as it may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when safe, then signal and return to your lane.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered line in most situations. Switch to a single-file line when turning, entering curves, or entering or exiting a highway.
